title: A session reads which paths other sessions hold from the backlog, not from messages
goal: backlog.py prints the touches of every claimed item with its claimer (and the claimer's sprint), so a session planning or orchestrating work learns which paths other sessions hold without asking them; the kb-sprint plan step names the command. Answers the SP-bno4xpft retrospective: path locks were negotiated by ad-hoc cross-session messages, one of which expired unread.

gates.question: Which command prints the paths claimed items hold?
options: a new subcommand: held [--overlaps ID] [--ref REF]
gates.recommendation: a new subcommand: held [--overlaps ID] [--ref REF]
gates.answer: a new subcommand: held [--overlaps ID] [--ref REF]

gates.question: Where does held read the claims of other sessions, and what does --overlaps exit with?
options: the item files by default, --ref REF (origin/main after git fetch) for every pushed claim; --overlaps exits 1 when it finds one
always origin/main; --overlaps exits 0 whatever it finds
